newsitem.title: UK: TR Technology agrees offer by new UK trust.
newsitem.headline: TR Technology agrees offer by new UK trust.

text.p: TR Technology Trust Plc (TRT) said on Friday that it had agreed reconstruction terms of its shares and package units with a new investment trust, Henderson Technology Trust (HTT).
TRT, which is due to be wound up on April 30, 1998, said it had always intended to allow shareholders to continue investment beyond the company's winding-up date.
Shareholders are being offered one HTT C share for each TRT ordinary share. After completion, The C share will be convertible into HTT ordinary shares and warrants.
Had the deal had been closed on October 29, TRT said 1,000 of its ordinary shares would have been worth 3431 HTT ordinary shares and 686 HTT warrants.

Either they can continue until 1998 with a highly-geared capital structure and an investment policy of progressively increasing the liquidity in the portfolio -- or maintain their exposure to the technology sector through ordinary shares and warrants in HTT with an ungeared capital structure, TRT said.

"The directors of TRT anticipate that the reduced risk associated with the HTT ordinary shares and C shares to be issued under the offers may result in such shares trading at a level closer to their underlying net asset value than is the case with the TRT ordinary shares," it stated.
Most of HTT's portfolio is expected to be invested medium and smaller sized technology stocks.

HTT, whose offer also extends to TRT stepped preference shares, TRT zero dividend preference shares, TRT package units, plans to raise up to 145.87 million stg via a placing and open offer for subscription of HTT ordinary shares and HTT warrants.
The offer values TRT ordinary shares at 304 pence, stepped preference shares at 160.5 pence, zero dividend preference shares at at 284.5 pence and package units at 3950 pence.
TRT said that the attributable asset values of the stepped preference shares and the zero dividend preference shares were around 154.66 pence and 263.82 pence respectively.
The trust is assuming acceptances for the offer for about 75 percent of its ordinary shares, 10 percent of the stepped preference shares and 10 percent of the zero dividend preference shares.
